title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the continuation of La Longue Marche. In it Grothendieck studies groups of automorphisms of the profinite fundamental group of the orbifold M_{1,1}, i.e. of (P)SL(2,Z)^, which is closely tied to π_{0,3}^ = π1(P^1 - {0,1,∞})^. He writes these groups M_{0,3}^~, S_0 M_{0,3}^~ and Γ_{0,3}^~. The equation des lacets constrains such an automorphism near the two elliptic points of the modular curve.
- ρ is the point j = 0, with stabiliser of order 6 and CM by Q(√-3) = Q(j). T_ρ = Res_{Q(ρ)/Q} G_m is the centraliser in GL2 of an element of order 3 (or 6).
- σ is the point j = 1728, with stabiliser of order 4 and CM by Q(i). T_σ is the corresponding torus and N'_σ ⊂ GL2 is its normaliser.
- G = GL2 and SG = SL2.
- M_{ρ,σ} ⊂ T_ρ × N'_σ × G is a group scheme of triples (a, b, u). On the previous page it is shown isomorphic to a quotient L_0 \ SΣ^×_{ρ,σ} of triples (α, β, f) = (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, u U^{-1}).
- The 'equation des lacets' (relations (4)) attaches to each automorphism a point of M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) mod Σ. This gives the homomorphisms (24) and (25).

This page.
- (26) On the subgroup 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} (§42 IV) the homomorphism (25) is a composite. First 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} ≃ SL(2,Ẑ)', the 'derived' subgroup, which is free on two generators, of index 12. Then this goes into SG(Ẑ)/(SG(Ẑ) ∩ Σ) = SL2(Ẑ)/±1 ⊂ M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ.
- (27) The embedding SG ↪ M_{ρ,σ} is u ↦ (1, 1, u), i.e. a = b = 1.
- (28)–(30) Σ = (Z/2)^3 = μ_2^3(Z). It sits centrally in M_{ρ,σ} through μ_2 ⊂ G_m, where G_m is the centre of T_ρ, of T_σ ⊂ N'_σ, and of G.
- (31)–(32) Dividing out the G-component gives Γ_{0,3}^~ → T_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/({±1}×{±1}). Here T_{ρ,σ} = {(a, b) ∈ T_ρ × N'_σ : det a / det b ∈ μ_2}. So the CM components a and b have the same determinant up to sign; both are essentially the cyclotomic-type character.
- The page ends by announcing the analysis of the four component homomorphisms (33)–(36) on the next page:
  - into B'_0(Ẑ), the Borel subgroup / cusp;
  - into GL2(Ẑ)/±1;
  - into the adelic units mod ±1 of Q(√-3);
  - into the adelic units mod ±1 of Q(i).

Purpose. The aim is to read off from the action on π1 of the modular orbifold explicit 'Galois-like' characters with values in the CM tori at the two orbifold points. This is a GT-type group mapping to adelic units of Q(√-3) and Q(i) in a compatible way, so the local monodromy data at j = 0 and j = 1728 become rigid group-theoretic invariants.
errors: (26) shows a hook arrow, i.e. claims injectivity, from 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} ≃ SL(2,Ẑ)' into SL2(Ẑ)/±1. If 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} is the full profinite completion of the free group SL(2,Z)', the map to the congruence completion is not injective, because SL2(Z) fails the congruence subgroup property. The statement is only correct if SL(2,Ẑ)' means the closure of SL(2,Z)' inside SL2(Ẑ). The notation is ambiguous, and the identification with 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} would then need justification.

The torus-intersection consistency checks out. -1 is not in the commutator subgroup of SL2(Z): its image in Z/12 is 6. Since SL2(Z)' is a congruence subgroup (level 6), -1 is also not in its closure, so SG(Ẑ) ∩ Σ = {±1} is not an issue for injectivity on the closure.
(32): 'Γμ_2' should be read as the global sections μ_2(Z) = {±1}. The condition is det a = ± det b, which is consistent with dividing by Σ_0 = {±1}×{±1}.

ideas.what: Encoding automorphisms of π1(M_{1,1})^ satisfying the loop equations as Ẑ-points of an algebraic group M_{ρ,σ} ⊂ T_ρ × N'_σ × GL2 built from CM tori at the two elliptic points
ideas.modern_name: GT-type / Galois action on profinite SL2(Z) with local data at elliptic points (j=0, 1728)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related: Nakamura (explicit Galois action on π1 of M_{1,1}), Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (GT and M_{1,1}/M_{1,2}, 1997), Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completions)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the 'Teichmüller tower' and M_{1,1} in general terms only

ideas.what: Homomorphisms from the Teichmüller-type automorphism group to the adelic units mod ±1 of Q(√-3) and Q(i), with det-compatibility det a = ± det b
ideas.modern_name: CM-type characters attached to orbifold points / inertia normalisers

ideas.what: Central μ_2^3 in M_{ρ,σ} and passage to quotients; embedding SL2 as a = b = 1

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, without completing it here, a homomorphism from the full 'Teichmüller-type' group Γ_{0,3}^~ into adelic CM tori of Q(√-3) and Q(i) (mod signs) with a determinant compatibility. This extends to the whole GT-like group what for Gal(Q̄/Q) would be the Hecke/CM characters at j = 0 and j = 1728. I know of no explicit such 'CM characters of GT' in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give GT-invariants detected by elliptic (orbifold) points rather than cusps. That bears on comparing GT with Gal(Q̄/Q), and on genus-one / elliptic GT (Enriquez's elliptic associators, Hain–Matsumoto).

missed.claim: Implicit link between the loop equations for M_{1,1} and CM theory (Hecke characters of Q(i), Q(√-3)) through the tori T_ρ and T_σ and the normaliser N'_σ.
missed.quote: T_ρ(Ẑ)/±1 (unités adéliques (mod ±1) du corps Q(j)) [next page]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could constrain or characterise the image of Galois in GT through behaviour at the CM points.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical setup step, but it documents an unpublished framework: a GT-type group acting on π1(M_{1,1})^ is mapped into adelic CM tori at the elliptic points. This seems not to have been worked out in the literature, though related themes are well studied (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto).
transcription_corrections: (26): the left group is the Gothic 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} (as on the previous page, 'Ĝ^{+λ}_{0,3}' should read 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3}), annotated '§42 IV'.
(27): under SG one reads 'SL(2, Z)' with the Z crossed out; '{+dans M_{ρ,σ},+}' is placed above the set {(a,b,u) | a = b = 1}.
(30): this is a diagram μ_2 ↪ G_m with three arrows to T_ρ, to T_σ → N'_σ, and to G, not a linear list.
(31): Γ_{0,3}^~ with a blotted subscript; Σ_0 underbraces {±1}×{±1}.
(32): the symbol is T_{ρ,σ} (curly T); 'Γμ_2' means the global sections of μ_2.
Archive page 481 corresponds to Grothendieck's own page numbering between 543 and 544 (likely 543 verso/bis).
